# Scholion

> Open-source, context-first version control that makes coding agents more productive. Each task is an isolated jj workspace; decisions, attempts (dead ends) and notes are stored as records anchored to code; a deterministic context pack gives any agent the context that matters without blowing up its context window or token budget. MIT licensed. The CLI is `scholion`, alias `av` (same program).

Source: https://github.com/vinhqbui/scholion
Status: an experiment, written almost entirely by coding agents with one human steering. Not audited infrastructure.

## Why

- Each new agent session spends tokens re-orienting: reading the tree, rediscovering what was tried, decided and rejected.
- Git keeps snapshots and drops intent, decisions and dead ends. A diff shows what changed, never why.
- Pasting more of the repo into the prompt doesn't help: the context window fills before the agent knows what matters.
- Scholion stores the "why" next to the code and hands any agent a context pack built from it: more relevant context, never more than the budget allows.

## Concepts

- Task: one unit of agent work (replaces branch + pull request), with its own jj workspace branched from trunk.
- Record: a typed note on a task: intent, decision, attempt, note, handoff, review. Summary <= 200 chars. Append-only; newer records supersede older ones.
- Anchor: a record's link to code (`path` or `path:Symbol`). The code hash is stored, so packs mark claims "(changed since recorded)".
- Convention: a repo rule scoped by path glob. Required conventions are always in the pack.
- Context pack: Markdown sections Task, Map, Decisions & dead ends, Code, Conventions, Live work, fitted to a token budget. No LLM; deterministic.
- Session ledger: what a session was already sent; later packs refer back ("↩ id (sent earlier)") instead of resending.
- Receipt: every pack is stored as `rcp:<8 hex>`.

## Use it from an agent

- MCP (any client): `claude mcp add --transport http av http://localhost:7420/mcp` — 24 tools including start_task, checkpoint, record, get_context, expand, handoff, claim_task, submit, merge, why, read_file, diff, log.
- Claude Code hooks: `integrations/claude-code/install.sh` (SessionStart pack, PostToolUse checkpoints).
- Anything else: `integrations/generic/av-wrap.sh <command…>` writes the pack to `$AV_CONTEXT_FILE`.

## Typical session

```bash
av task start --repo api --title "Add retry" --goal "retry embedder calls with backoff"
cd ~/ws/api/add-retry
av record --kind attempt --summary "tried tenacity; not installed" --anchor shared/text.py
av context --budget 4000
av handoff --done "retries added" --remaining "tests for the 429 path"
av submit
```

## Evidence (reproducible, in the repo)

- Retrieval E1, 42 tasks from 6 public repos, 4000-token budget: the pack shows code for 0.91 of the gold files (BM25 over symbols 0.89, repo map 0.68, BM25 over files 0.44). `bench/retrieval/`
- Claude Code + Haiku, 40 sessions per arm, small Python repo: turns −12.9% at unchanged cost (±0.0%); input tokens +5.9% vs plain git. `bench/results/2026-10-27-haiku/`
- Not yet shown: the productivity gain on large codebases. The 20k-line Rust task set is unmeasured.

## Contribute

Rust 2024, Cargo workspace. TDD: failing test first, then `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`. See CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md in the repo.

Open problems:
- Run the medium benchmark (`bench/tasks-scholion`, ~1 GB disk per session).
- Add tree-sitter languages to `crates/scholion-index` (Rust, TypeScript, Python today).
- Hooks for more agents (Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Aider) in `integrations/`.
- Fit more relevant context into the same budget in `crates/scholion-pack`.
- Real agent identity (agent names are self-asserted today).
- Use it on a real repo and file issues: https://github.com/vinhqbui/scholion/issues
